root_cause: The radios component only listens for 'click' events on its module element. Keyboard navigation (ArrowDown) changes the checked radio via native browser behavior, which fires a 'change' event on the radio input but not a 'click' event. Since the two radio groups (channel-radios and optout-radios) are separate modules but share the same 'name' attribute, selecting the opt-out radio in one module unchecks the text-message radio in the other module without the first module receiving any event, so its conditional field remains visible.
repair_strategy: Add a document-level 'change' event listener in each Radios instance that filters for radio inputs sharing any name used by that instance's radios. When such a change occurs, invoke the existing handleClick logic to update all conditional reveals in that module. This ensures keyboard, mouse, and assistive-tech selections all update visibility correctly, even across module boundaries.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all radio options using arrow keys and see conditional fields show/hide appropriately across module boundaries, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Both click and change events may fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent, so no adverse effect.
Multiple Radios instances on the same page will each add a document change listener; they filter by name so only relevant changes trigger handleClick.
The handler only processes inputs with type radio and an aria-controls attribute, preventing unintended side effects on other form fields.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Email radio to the Text message radio shows the mobile number field.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Text message radio to the Opt‑out radio hides the mobile number field.
Verify that clicking a radio with mouse still updates the conditional content correctly.
Verify that pressing Space on a focused radio updates the conditional content.
Ensure no JavaScript errors are thrown in the console during these interactions.
